operators.name: Literal definition node
operators.definition: A geometry, topology, operator, profile or schedule is stored as a typed definition record inside the substrate.

operators.name: Content-addressed definition
operators.definition: Canonical UTF-8 JSON, excluding the hash field itself, is hashed with SHA-256 to make definition identity verifiable.

operators.name: Explicit dependency edge
operators.definition: Every composed definition lists definition IDs it depends on; hidden imports and implicit global state are forbidden.

operators.name: Versioned namespace
operators.definition: Definition IDs include stable namespaces while schema_version and profile_version separate compatible from incompatible semantics.

operators.name: Definition-instance separation
operators.definition: A definition describes an operator or shape family; an instance supplies literal parameters and state through definition_ref.

operators.name: Acyclic resolution rule
operators.definition: Definition dependency graphs must be acyclic unless a future fixed-point kind declares bounds, tolerance and termination.

operators.name: Typed implicit-field sign
operators.definition: An implicit field declares domain, codomain and sign convention: negative interior, zero boundary, positive exterior.

operators.name: Exact-SDF capability flag
operators.definition: Exact signed-distance status is a capability that only valid primitives and distance-preserving transforms may claim.

operators.name: Parametric curve and sweep
operators.definition: A curve gamma(u) and a frame or transport rule may generate a swept surface; parameter interval and regularity are explicit.

operators.name: Pulse polygon embedding
operators.definition: m declared pulses map to a point, segment or regular m-gon; for m=3 the result is a triangle.

operators.name: Radix shell chart
operators.definition: Digit thresholds b^k form exact scale boundaries and may index nested shells without implying that space is inherently radix-based.

operators.name: Log-polar core chart
operators.definition: rho=ln(r/r0), theta=atan2(y,x) is local and carries an explicit core/singularity flag.

operators.name: Explicit quotient/gluing map
operators.definition: Topology is represented by boundary ports, coordinate maps, orientation transport and optional sheet changes.

operators.name: Sheet-aware co-location
operators.definition: Equal coordinates do not imply equality or coupling; sheet, phase, orientation, branch and policy remain typed state.

operators.name: Orientation transport
operators.definition: Orientation is propagated independently and flips only at declared maps or transitions.

operators.name: Port and branch routing
operators.definition: A guarded crossing selects an explicit output port and branch; the routing table is finite and inspectable.

operators.name: Split-merge lineage
operators.definition: Splits create child addresses and merges record all parents; coordinates never replace durable identity.

operators.name: Guarded topology change
operators.definition: A morph may vary continuously, but a topology-class change commits only at an event with a declared guard and transition.

operators.name: Generic hinge tuple
operators.definition: A hinge is H=(pivot,state,map,guard,invariant) with typed continuous or discrete state.

operators.name: Continuous planar hinge
operators.definition: A continuous hinge uses an affine rotation about a fixed pivot; velocity follows the derivative of the transform.

operators.name: Discrete parity hinge
operators.definition: A one-bit state selects one of two declared maps or routes and does not carry full geometry or identity.

operators.name: Connector hinge
operators.definition: A zero-magnitude connector can be topologically necessary in an ordered parse graph, as with Dutch en.

operators.name: Non-commutative hinge chain
operators.definition: Composition order is explicit because H2∘H1 generally differs from H1∘H2.

operators.name: Invariant subspace contract
operators.definition: A hinge may declare fixed points, axes or quantities; the runtime validates them instead of inferring invariance from a name.

operators.name: Bounded Dutch number profile
operators.definition: A versioned lexicon covers standard 0..99 orthography, pronunciation-like segments, morphemes and hinge metadata.

operators.name: Syllable-pulse operator
operators.definition: Each declared pronunciation segment emits one pulse; dialect and tokenizer are profile metadata.

operators.name: Teen suffix hinge
operators.definition: For regular 13..19 forms, the unit root precedes tien although decimal place semantics are ten plus unit.

operators.name: En connector hinge
operators.definition: For non-multiple tens 21..99, spoken morphology is unit-en-tens while numeral place order is tens-unit.

operators.name: Spoken-place permutation
operators.definition: The place tuple and spoken tuple are separate charts connected by an explicit permutation plus optional connector node.

operators.name: Feature-count comparison
operators.definition: Binary popcount and phonetic pulse count may be compared; equality is tagged as a coincidence, never numeric identity.

operators.name: Phase-ordered evaluator
operators.definition: The canonical order is parse, normalize, resolve, construct, transform, support, compatibility, guard, transition, lineage.

operators.name: Support-compatibility-guard discipline
operators.definition: Cheap local support precedes compatibility; event solving occurs only after both gates admit a candidate.

operators.name: Deterministic trace
operators.definition: Each pipeline step records definition ID, operator kind and typed output to make order and provenance inspectable.

operators.name: Evidence disposition
operators.definition: Every source-derived or newly inferred mechanism is labeled RETAIN, ENGINEERING, CORRECTED, BOUNDED, DEMOTE or REJECT.

operators.name: Unknown-reference and cycle rejection
operators.definition: Loading fails on missing definition IDs, duplicate IDs, invalid hashes or cyclic dependencies.

operators.name: Package verification contract
operators.definition: Schema validation, executable tests, source hashes, file hashes and a reproducible demo accompany the PDF.
